executiveVerdict.headline: Statement #1 dominates 58.0% of total execution cost (18.45 subtree cost).
executiveVerdict.summary: Primary Bottleneck: Statement #1 creates temporary tables via SELECT ... INTO as unindexed heaps, triggering repeated nested loops and missing index penalties in downstream statements. Additionally, query execution is constrained to a single CPU core (MaxDOP = 1).
executiveVerdict.actionableFix: Pre-create temporary tables using explicit CREATE TABLE #temp (...) with a CLUSTERED PRIMARY KEY on join keys before inserting data.

antiPatterns.title: Implicit Data Type Conversions
antiPatterns.description: SQL Server is performing CONVERT_IMPLICIT on column expressions, invalidating index seeks and distorting cardinality estimations.
antiPatterns.recommendation: Align parameter and variable data types with the underlying column data types (e.g. check INT vs SMALLINT/TINYINT or VARCHAR vs NVARCHAR).

antiPatterns.title: Heap Table RID Lookups
antiPatterns.description: Target tables have no Clustered Index (Heap), forcing costly RID lookups on every row retrieved.
antiPatterns.recommendation: Define a Clustered Index on the primary key or high-frequency lookup columns of the table.

antiPatterns.title: Single Threaded Execution (MaxDOP = 1)
antiPatterns.description: The query plan is forced to run on a single CPU core because MaxDOP is set to 1 at the server, database, or resource governor level.
antiPatterns.recommendation: Consider setting Cost Threshold for Parallelism (e.g. 50) and MAXDOP based on NUMA core architecture rather than forcing MAXDOP 1 globally.

antiPatterns.title: Heavy Key / RID Lookups
antiPatterns.description: Index seeks are followed by thousands of per-row lookups into the base table to fetch columns the index does not contain.
antiPatterns.recommendation: Add the fetched columns to the driving index with INCLUDE, or create a covering index.

antiPatterns.title: Columns With No Statistics
antiPatterns.description: The optimizer compiled this plan without statistics on filtered/joined columns and used guessed selectivity.
antiPatterns.recommendation: Enable AUTO_CREATE_STATISTICS and create the listed statistics (CREATE STATISTICS ... WITH FULLSCAN).

antiPatterns.title: Parameter Sniffing Mismatch
antiPatterns.description: The plan was compiled for parameter values that differ from the runtime values.
antiPatterns.recommendation: Use OPTION (RECOMPILE), OPTIMIZE FOR UNKNOWN, split skewed paths, or SQL Server 2022 PSP optimization.

antiPatterns.title: Non-Sargable Predicates
antiPatterns.description: Functions wrapped around indexed columns (or leading-wildcard LIKE) block index seeks and force row-by-row evaluation.
antiPatterns.recommendation: Rewrite predicates so the bare column is compared to a computed constant/range, or add an indexed computed column.

implicitConversions.description: CONVERT_IMPLICIT on CONVERT_IMPLICIT(nvarchar(20),[c].[RegionCode],0) forces per-row conversion, disabling Sargable index seeks.
implicitConversions.remedy: Match application parameter/variable datatype exactly with underlying column definition.

implicitConversions.description: Internal implicit datatype casting detected in query execution predicate.
implicitConversions.remedy: Ensure variables and column schemas share identical datatypes and collations.

cardinalityEngine.description: Query compiled under Modern Cardinality Estimator (Model Version 150).
cardinalityEngine.remedy: Ensure table statistics have adequate sample rates for multi-column join correlation.

keyLookups.description: Key Lookup on [dbo].[OrderItems] is performed ~4200 time(s): each row found by the index seek requires an extra random read into the base table to fetch 3 column(s) the index does not contain.
keyLookups.remedy: Add the fetched columns to the existing index [IX_OrderItems_OrderID]: INCLUDE ([ProductID], [Quantity], [UnitPrice]). At this volume the optimizer may soon abandon the index entirely for a full scan (tipping point).

spools.description: Eager Spool under a data-modification operator: the engine fully materializes the rows to be changed so the update cannot re-read rows it already modified.
spools.remedy: Normally harmless. If expensive, avoid reading and modifying the same index key (e.g. UPDATE ... SET key = key + 1), or modify through a different index/staging table.

missingStatistics.description: The optimizer had NO statistics on [Status] of [dbo].[Orders], so it guessed selectivity (fixed 10%/30% heuristics). Row estimates, join order and memory grants are unreliable.
missingStatistics.remedy: Ensure AUTO_CREATE_STATISTICS is ON (and the DB is not read-only), then create/refresh the statistics. Auto-creation is skipped for read-only databases, some column types, and when disabled.

parameterSniffing.description: Classic parameter sniffing: the cached plan was built for different values than this execution (@RegionCode compiled for N'US-EAST', ran with N'EU-WEST') and the cardinality estimates are visibly wrong for the runtime values.
parameterSniffing.remedy: Options: OPTION (RECOMPILE) for volatile/skewed predicates; OPTION (OPTIMIZE FOR UNKNOWN) or OPTIMIZE FOR (@p = typical) for a stable generic plan; split skewed branches into separate procedures; SQL Server 2022 Parameter Sensitive Plan optimization; or force a good plan via Query Store.

nonSargable.description: Predicate applies DATEPART() to an indexed column. This hides the column from index seeks (non-sargable): the expression is evaluated row by row during a scan. Table: Orders.
nonSargable.remedy: Rewrite date-part filters as a half-open range: WHERE col >= '2024-01-01' AND col < '2025-01-01'.

pleRiskReport.headline: High Buffer Pool Ingestion (Elevated PLE Threat)
pleRiskReport.summary: Query ingests ~475.0 MB of data pages into memory. If executed repeatedly in high-concurrency environments, this will cause frequent PLE drops and disk I/O stalls.
